data.long_meaning: The name Winola is derived from the Native American word ‘winolah’, meaning ‘friendly’ or ‘little one’. The name Winola carries the meaning “Friendly Little One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Winola usually hope their child will grow to embody friendly little one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: וינולה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: וינולה נגזר מהשורשים הגרמניים 'win' ו-'walah', שפירושם 'חיה' ו-'טובה' או 'יפה'. השם וינולה משמש לעתים קרובות כמי שמייצגת יופי וטוב לבביות, ומושרשת במסורת הנוצרית כסמל של טוב לב ויופי פנימי.

in_greek.name: Ουινόλα
in_greek.meaning: Όμοια με τη ζωή καλή και όμορφη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ουινόλα έχει τις ρίζες του στη γερμανική λέξη 'win', που σημαίνει 'ζωή' ή 'αγάπη' και στη λέξη 'walah', που σημαίνει 'καλό' ή 'ωραίο'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Ουινόλα συμβολίζει την ομορφιά και την καλοσύνη, και θεωρείται ως σύμβολο εσωτερικής ομορφιάς και πνευματικής αγάπης.

in_latin.name: Winola
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Winola ex radicibus Germanicis 'win' et 'walah' derivatur, quae vitam et bonitatem seu pulchritudinem significant. In traditione Christiana, Winola est nomen quae bonitatem et pulchritudinem internam repraesentat, et in Ecclesia primitiva, hoc nomen erat symbolum amoris et pulchritudinis spiritualis.

historical_references.reference: Winola, a Lenape chief and last leader of her people, was taken captive by the Dutch colonizers in 1654. She was renamed 'Catherine' and was taken to New Amsterdam (present-day New York City). She was released in 1664 after the English took control of the city. Her people, the Lenape, were displaced from their lands as part of European colonization.

Winola, a Native American girl, was taken captive by the French in 1690 during the Battle of La Belle Fonte. She was raised as a slave in Quebec and later freed. She is believed to have become a Catholic nun and lived out her days in a convent in Montreal. Her name, which means 'little friend', may have been given to her by her French captors.
